title: Sanders favorability is rescaled twice
published: The estimated slope of 0.034 indicates that an ad achieving the maximum rating of 1 relative to the minimum rating of 0 would be 3.4 points higher.
corrected: The estimated slope of [[0.044]] indicates that an ad achieving the maximum rating of 1 relative to the minimum rating of 0 would be [[4.4]] points higher.
note: `clean_exps.R` applies `(favorBS_rev - 1)/4` twice, so Sanders favorability runs from -0.25 to 0 where the other candidates run from 0 to 1, and the 12 favorability estimates for the two pro-Sanders ads are a quarter of their size. The slope stays significant. The same rows enter Figure 2, where 0.014 (0.017) becomes 0.008 (0.034) and 0.008 (0.014) becomes 0.026 (0.025), and Figure 3, where -0.004 (0.013) becomes -0.012 (0.021). Tables C.1, C.6, C.11, and E.17 hold the same rows, and refitting them changes 102 of their 152 printed coefficients and standard errors, in the 5 columns that include the Sanders ads. Stars move on 10 coefficients. On the index coefficient the moves are C.6 Dem (PD), 0.052\* to 0.021, E.17 Ind (PD), 0.223 to 0.507\*, and E.17 All (2), 0.036 to 0.050\*. No Figure 2 or 3 slope becomes distinguishable from zero. Both accuracy scripts repeat the same line, and there a CATE's scale can change which ad wins a matchup. Rerunning them without the line changes 12 of the 56 favorability and vote choice statistics behind Figures E.11 and E.12, all on favorability. In Figure E.11 the overall estimate, 0.508 becomes 0.502, and the Democrats' estimate, 0.578 becomes 0.564. In Figure E.12 the overall estimate, 0.489 becomes 0.444, and the Democrats' estimate, 0.733 becomes 0.667. Both Democrats' intervals exclude 0.50 as published and contain it once corrected. The overall individual intervals still contain 0.50, so the appendix's conclusion that individuals are no better than random guessing stands.

title: Turnout and issue estimates take the sign of the ad's valence
location: p. 11, Figure 4, the label in each panel; the data are also in app. Tables C.3 to C.5, C.8 to C.10, and C.13 to C.15
published: Target Issue Support, Negative Index: [[0.052 (0.059)]]. Turnout Intentions, Negative Index: [[-0.017 (0.021)]]. Target Issue Support, Positive Index: [[-0.039 (0.041)]]. Turnout Intentions, Positive Index: [[0.064 (0.035)]].
corrected: Target Issue Support, Negative Index: [[0.018 (0.072)]]. Turnout Intentions, Negative Index: [[0.017 (0.021)]]. Target Issue Support, Positive Index: [[-0.053 (0.042)]]. Turnout Intentions, Positive Index: [[-0.052 (0.028)]].
note: `estimate_all_cates.R` multiplies every outcome by -1 for an anti ad, which suits candidate favorability and vote choice. It also flips turnout, so an anti ad that raises turnout plots as lowering it, in 90 of 102 estimates. For issues the deposit's `ad_id_to_base_by_hand.csv` carries a `direction` column that no script reads, and it disagrees with the sign used in 63 of 102 estimates. The corrected labels refit the same CATEs with no flip on turnout and with `direction` on issues (`maintained/corrected_slopes.R`). This correction counts a rise in turnout intentions as a rise whichever candidate the ad attacks, although an ad might be meant to demobilize. All four slopes remain indistinguishable from zero, so the sentence on p. 10 that the slopes of all four meta-regression lines are close to zero and not statistically significant stands. The appendix tables were not refit, and their turnout and issue columns carry the published signs.
